readerValues.programmeDescription: Chinese Studies at Leiden combines Mandarin and Classical Chinese with the study of China’s history, culture, politics, economy and society. Students develop language and research skills, normally spend a period studying Mandarin in China or Taiwan, and complete an independent paper linked to a third-year seminar. Elective choices allow a disciplinary emphasis; these are not separate formal specialisations.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: No close UCR comparison was found for this documented Chinese Studies curriculum. UCR has relevant historical, political, economic and cultural courses, but its strongest combinations do not sustain the programme’s China-centered inquiry. The unresolved language-choice allocation is shown separately from this academic judgment.

curriculum.routeLabel: Chinese Studies; political economy and society choices
curriculum.limitation: The listed requirements total 175 EC and include 30 EC of elective space. A further language choice is required, but the official rules disagree about whether it is 5 EC overall or 5 EC in each semester. The paper and its linked seminar are counted together as 10 EC. This is an incomplete curriculum, not a certified 180-EC degree plan.

componentNotes.y2-mandarin-2c-abroad: One 15-EC language-training period in China or Taiwan. Participation requires the completed first year and the applicable cohort and departure conditions. A programme in Leiden is available only under specified circumstances.
componentNotes.y3-ba-paper: The linked seminar and independent paper together carry 10 EC. A completed first year, permission and supervision arrangements are required.
componentNotes.y3-elective-space: 30 EC of elective space, subject to Leiden’s requirements. The Chinese Economy and Society minor cannot be used because of overlap with compulsory study.

comparisonScope.label: No close UCR comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The 24 documented components totaling 175 EC, including 30 EC of genuine open study and the integrated 10-EC paper and seminar. Known language, historical, cultural, social and political-economic teaching all inform the judgment.
comparisonScope.excluded: The disputed third-year language-choice allocation of 5 EC overall versus two 5-EC choices, full cohort progression and future eligibility for the China/Taiwan period. The documented subset is not a certified complete 180-EC degree plan.
